verses.text: Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth!

blocks.text: Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth!

verses.text: Draw me after you; let us run.

blocks.text: Draw me after you; let us run.

we will extol your love more than wine;

She

verses.text: I am very dark, but lovely,

blocks.text: I am very dark, but lovely,

verses.text: Do not gaze at me because I am dark,

blocks.text: Do not gaze at me because I am dark,

My mother’s sons were angry with me;

verses.text: Tell me, you whom my soul loves,

blocks.text: Tell me, you whom my soul loves,

verses.text: As a lily among brambles,

verses.text: As an apple tree among the trees of the forest,

blocks.text: As an apple tree among the trees of the forest,

and his fruit was sweet to my taste.

verses.text: He brought me to the banqueting house,

blocks.text: He brought me to the banqueting house,

verses.text: Sustain me with raisins;

blocks.text: Sustain me with raisins;

verses.text: His left hand is under my head,

The Bride Adores Her Beloved

verses.text: The voice of my beloved!

blocks.text: The voice of my beloved!
Behold, he comes,
leaping over the mountains,
bounding over the hills.

verses.text: My beloved is like a gazelle

blocks.text: My beloved is like a gazelle
or a young stag.
Behold, there he stands
behind our wall,
gazing through the windows,
looking through the lattice.

verses.text: My beloved speaks and says to me:

blocks.text: My beloved speaks and says to me:
“Arise, my love, my beautiful one,
and come away,

verses.text: for behold, the winter is past;

blocks.text: for behold, the winter is past;
the rain is over and gone.

verses.text: The flowers appear on the earth,

blocks.text: The flowers appear on the earth,
the time of singing has come,
and the voice of the turtledove
is heard in our land.

verses.text: The fig tree ripens its figs,

blocks.text: The fig tree ripens its figs,
and the vines are in blossom;
they give forth fragrance.
Arise, my love, my beautiful one,
and come away.

verses.text: O my dove, in the clefts of the rock,

blocks.text: O my dove, in the clefts of the rock,
in the crannies of the cliff,
let me see your face,
let me hear your voice,
for your voice is sweet,
and your face is lovely.

verses.text: Catch the foxes for us,

blocks.text: Catch the foxes for us,
the little foxes
that spoil the vineyards,
for our vineyards are in blossom.”

verses.text: My beloved is mine, and I am his;

blocks.text: My beloved is mine, and I am his;
he grazes among the lilies.

verses.text: Until the day breathes

blocks.text: Until the day breathes
and the shadows flee,

or a young stag on cleft mountains.
The Bride’s Dream

verses.text: On my bed by night

blocks.text: On my bed by night
I sought him whom my soul loves;
I sought him, but found him not.

verses.text: I will rise now and go about the city,

blocks.text: I will rise now and go about the city,
in the streets and in the squares;
I will seek him whom my soul loves.
I sought him, but found him not.

verses.text: The watchmen found me

blocks.text: The watchmen found me
as they went about in the city.
“Have you seen him whom my soul loves?”

verses.text: Scarcely had I passed them

blocks.text: Scarcely had I passed them
when I found him whom my soul loves.
I held him, and would not let him go
until I had brought him into my mother’s house,
and into the chamber of her who conceived me.

Solomon Arrives for the Wedding

verses.text: What is that coming up from the wilderness

blocks.text: What is that coming up from the wilderness
like columns of smoke,
perfumed with myrrh and frankincense,
with all the fragrant powders of a merchant?

verses.text: Behold, it is the litter of Solomon!

blocks.text: Behold, it is the litter of Solomon!
Around it are sixty mighty men,
some of the mighty men of Israel,

verses.text: all of them wearing swords

blocks.text: all of them wearing swords
and expert in war,
each with his sword at his thigh,
against terror by night.

verses.text: King Solomon made himself a carriage

blocks.text: King Solomon made himself a carriage
from the wood of Lebanon.

verses.text: He made its posts of silver,

blocks.text: He made its posts of silver,
its back of gold, its seat of purple;
its interior was inlaid with love
by the daughters of Jerusalem.

verses.text: Go out, O daughters of Zion,

blocks.text: Go out, O daughters of Zion,
and look upon King Solomon,
with the crown with which his mother crowned him
on the day of his wedding,
on the day of the gladness of his heart.
Solomon Admires His Bride’s Beauty
He

verses.text: Behold, you are beautiful, my love,

blocks.text: Behold, you are beautiful, my love,
behold, you are beautiful!
Your eyes are doves
behind your veil.
Your hair is like a flock of goats
leaping down the slopes of Gilead.

verses.text: Your teeth are like a flock of shorn ewes

blocks.text: Your teeth are like a flock of shorn ewes
that have come up from the washing,
all of which bear twins,
and not one among them has lost its young.

verses.text: Your lips are like a scarlet thread,

blocks.text: Your lips are like a scarlet thread,
and your mouth is lovely.
Your cheeks are like halves of a pomegranate
behind your veil.

verses.text: Your neck is like the tower of David,

blocks.text: Your neck is like the tower of David,
built in rows of stone;
on it hang a thousand shields,
all of them shields of warriors.

verses.text: Your two breasts are like two fawns,

blocks.text: Your two breasts are like two fawns,
twins of a gazelle,
that graze among the lilies.

verses.text: Until the day breathes

blocks.text: Until the day breathes
and the shadows flee,
I will go away to the mountain of myrrh
and the hill of frankincense.

verses.text: You are altogether beautiful, my love;

blocks.text: You are altogether beautiful, my love;
there is no flaw in you.

verses.text: Come with me from Lebanon, my bride;

blocks.text: Come with me from Lebanon, my bride;
come with me from Lebanon.
Depart from the peak of Amana,
from the peak of Senir and Hermon,
from the dens of lions,
from the mountains of leopards.

verses.text: You have captivated my heart, my sister, my bride;

blocks.text: You have captivated my heart, my sister, my bride;
you have captivated my heart with one glance of your eyes,
with one jewel of your necklace.

verses.text: How beautiful is your love, my sister, my bride!

blocks.text: How beautiful is your love, my sister, my bride!
How much better is your love than wine,
and the fragrance of your oils than any spice!

verses.text: Your lips drip nectar, my bride;

blocks.text: Your lips drip nectar, my bride;
honey and milk are under your tongue;
the fragrance of your garments is like the fragrance of Lebanon.

verses.text: A garden locked is my sister, my bride,

blocks.text: A garden locked is my sister, my bride,
a spring locked, a fountain sealed.

verses.text: Your shoots are an orchard of pomegranates

blocks.text: Your shoots are an orchard of pomegranates
with all choicest fruits,
henna with nard,

verses.text: nard and saffron, calamus and cinnamon,

blocks.text: nard and saffron, calamus and cinnamon,
with all trees of frankincense,
myrrh and aloes,
with all choice spices—

verses.text: a garden fountain, a well of living water,

blocks.text: a garden fountain, a well of living water,
and flowing streams from Lebanon.

verses.text: Awake, O north wind,

blocks.text: Awake, O north wind,
and come, O south wind!
Blow upon my garden,
let its spices flow.
Together in the Garden of Love
She
Let my beloved come to his garden,
and eat its choicest fruits.
He

verses.text: I came to my garden, my sister, my bride,

blocks.text: I came to my garden, my sister, my bride,
I gathered my myrrh with my spice,

Others
Eat, friends, drink,
and be drunk with love!
The Bride Searches for Her Beloved
She

verses.text: I slept, but my heart was awake.

blocks.text: I slept, but my heart was awake.
A sound! My beloved is knocking.
“Open to me, my sister, my love,
my dove, my perfect one,
for my head is wet with dew,
my locks with the drops of the night.”

verses.text: I had put off my garment;

blocks.text: I had put off my garment;
how could I put it on?
I had bathed my feet;
how could I soil them?

verses.text: My beloved put his hand to the latch,

blocks.text: My beloved put his hand to the latch,
and my heart was thrilled within me.

verses.text: I arose to open to my beloved,

blocks.text: I arose to open to my beloved,
and my hands dripped with myrrh,
my fingers with liquid myrrh,
on the handles of the bolt.

verses.text: I opened to my beloved,

blocks.text: I opened to my beloved,
but my beloved had turned and gone.
My soul failed me when he spoke.
I sought him, but found him not;
I called him, but he gave no answer.

verses.text: The watchmen found me

blocks.text: The watchmen found me
as they went about in the city;
they beat me, they bruised me,
they took away my veil,
those watchmen of the walls.

verses.text: I adjure you, O daughters of Jerusalem,

blocks.text: I adjure you, O daughters of Jerusalem,
if you find my beloved,

I am sick with love.

verses.text: What is your beloved more than another beloved,

blocks.text: What is your beloved more than another beloved,
O most beautiful among women?

The Bride Praises Her Beloved
She

verses.text: My beloved is radiant and ruddy,

blocks.text: My beloved is radiant and ruddy,
distinguished among ten thousand.

verses.text: His head is the finest gold;

blocks.text: His head is the finest gold;
his locks are wavy,
black as a raven.

verses.text: His eyes are like doves

blocks.text: His eyes are like doves

bathed in milk,
sitting beside a full pool.

verses.text: His cheeks are like beds of spices,

blocks.text: His cheeks are like beds of spices,
mounds of sweet-smelling herbs.
His lips are lilies,
dripping liquid myrrh.

verses.text: His arms are rods of gold,

blocks.text: His arms are rods of gold,
set with jewels.
His body is polished ivory,
bedecked with sapphires.

verses.text: His legs are alabaster columns,

blocks.text: His legs are alabaster columns,
set on bases of gold.
His appearance is like Lebanon,
choice as the cedars.

verses.text: His mouth is most sweet,

blocks.text: His mouth is most sweet,
and he is altogether desirable.
This is my beloved and this is my friend,

Others

verses.text: Where has your beloved gone,

blocks.text: Where has your beloved gone,
O most beautiful among women?
Where has your beloved turned,

Together in the Garden of Love
She

verses.text: My beloved has gone down to his garden

blocks.text: My beloved has gone down to his garden
to the beds of spices,

and to gather lilies.

verses.text: I am my beloved’s and my beloved is mine;

blocks.text: I am my beloved’s and my beloved is mine;

He

verses.text: You are beautiful as Tirzah, my love,

blocks.text: You are beautiful as Tirzah, my love,

verses.text: Turn away your eyes from me,

blocks.text: Turn away your eyes from me,

verses.text: Your teeth are like a flock of ewes

blocks.text: Your teeth are like a flock of ewes

verses.text: My dove, my perfect one, is the only one,

blocks.text: My dove, my perfect one, is the only one,

verses.text: “Who is this who looks down like the dawn,

blocks.text: “Who is this who looks down like the dawn,

blocks.text: I went down to the nut orchard

verses.text: Before I was aware, my desire set me

blocks.text: Before I was aware, my desire set me

verses.text: Return, return, O Shulammite,

blocks.text: Return, return, O Shulammite,

as upon a dance before two armies?

verses.text: How beautiful are your feet in sandals,

blocks.text: How beautiful are your feet in sandals,
O noble daughter!
Your rounded thighs are like jewels,
the work of a master hand.

verses.text: Your navel is a rounded bowl

blocks.text: Your navel is a rounded bowl

Your belly is a heap of wheat,

verses.text: Your two breasts are like two fawns,

blocks.text: Your two breasts are like two fawns,

verses.text: Your neck is like an ivory tower.

blocks.text: Your neck is like an ivory tower.
Your eyes are pools in Heshbon,
by the gate of Bath-rabbim.

verses.text: Your head crowns you like Carmel,

blocks.text: Your head crowns you like Carmel,

verses.text: How beautiful and pleasant you are,

blocks.text: How beautiful and pleasant you are,

verses.text: Your stature is like a palm tree,

blocks.text: Your stature is like a palm tree,
and your breasts are like its clusters.

verses.text: I say I will climb the palm tree

blocks.text: I say I will climb the palm tree
and lay hold of its fruit.
Oh may your breasts be like clusters of the vine,
and the scent of your breath like apples,

verses.text: and your mouth like the best wine.

blocks.text: and your mouth like the best wine.

It goes down smoothly for my beloved,
gliding over lips and teeth.

verses.text: I am my beloved’s,

blocks.text: I am my beloved’s,

verses.text: Come, my beloved,

blocks.text: Come, my beloved,

verses.text: let us go out early to the vineyards

blocks.text: let us go out early to the vineyards
and see whether the vines have budded,
whether the grape blossoms have opened
and the pomegranates are in bloom.
There I will give you my love.

verses.text: The mandrakes give forth fragrance,

blocks.text: The mandrakes give forth fragrance,

verses.text: Oh that you were like a brother to me

blocks.text: Oh that you were like a brother to me

and none would despise me.

verses.text: I would lead you and bring you

blocks.text: I would lead you and bring you
into the house of my mother—
she who used to teach me.
I would give you spiced wine to drink,
the juice of my pomegranate.

verses.text: His left hand is under my head,

verses.text: Who is that coming up from the wilderness,

Under the apple tree I awakened you.

verses.text: Set me as a seal upon your heart,

blocks.text: Set me as a seal upon your heart,
as a seal upon your arm,
for love is strong as death,
jealousy is fierce as the grave.

the very flame of the LORD.

verses.text: Many waters cannot quench love,

blocks.text: Many waters cannot quench love,

verses.text: We have a little sister,

blocks.text: We have a little sister,

verses.text: If she is a wall,

blocks.text: If she is a wall,

verses.text: I was a wall,

blocks.text: I was a wall,

verses.text: Solomon had a vineyard at Baal-hamon;

blocks.text: Solomon had a vineyard at Baal-hamon;

verses.text: My vineyard, my very own, is before me;

verses.text: O you who dwell in the gardens,
